Dear Honorable Mayor, Councilmembers and City Manager,

I hope this emailfinds you well and in good spirits.

I'm writing on behalf of a coalition of community leaders from the San Gabriel Valley. This past weekend, in
response to the growing concerns over the COVID-19 pandemic, community organizers from the San Gabriel
Valley joined a call to address the following question: How do we protect our most vulnerable communities
during the COVID-19 pandemic?

The result is the affached letter with a list of recommendations from over 120 San Gabriel Valley community
organizers and leaders. We hope this document is helpful as you take steps to address this crisis. We
understand that these recommendations may have been addressed by Governor Gavin Newsom within the
last 24 hours, and look to our cities for updates on how these policies will be implemented with fidelity.

Thank you for all of your continued efforts to keep our communities healthy during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions, comments or concerns.

ln solidarity,
Jennifer

   Updated: March 16,2020
Dear Honorable Mayor, Councilmembers and City Manager,

As leaders in the San Gabriel Valley, we are committed to ensuring equitable outcomes for the most vulnerable
members of our community during this unprecedented crisis.

We appreciate the brave leadership of local leaders who have made efforts to postpone or cancel public events,
close public facilities, and support the closure of schools. We recognize the myriad of challenges facing our
elected officials at this time.

Local govemments in partnership with state and federal government and other stakeholders can reduce risk and
harm during a natural disaster as is the current COVID-I9 pandemic. Public health literature identifies
disproportionate consequences to vulnerable subpopulations including women and children, workers, and
immigrants/migrants.

We recommend the following in order to support our most vulnerable communities in the San Gabriel Valley:

  a  Secure and Safe Housing: Halt all evictions and ban utility shutoffs for all residents impacted by
  COVID-I9. Distribute rental assistance and prohibit rent increases for impacted residents.
  a  Equitable Economic Relief: Provide financial relief for mom-and-pop businesses. Expand paid leave for
  all school, municipal and state employees impacted by COVID-I9. Ensure equitable distribution of state
  and federal relief monies. Distribute information to ensure all residents have access to state
  unemployment resources.
  Compassionate, Centralized Social Services: Disperse list of local providers offering meal services and
  identify locations for emergency childcare. Ensure technology needs for low-income students are met
  through partnerships with community-based organizations.
  o  Outreach and Education: Be accessible as local leaders to provide COVID-l9 fact-based and
  community-appropriate messaging. Wellness check-ins over the phone or in-person for isolated,
  vulnerable seniors. IJtilize existing partnerships to reach residents where they are. Combat health
  misinformation by providing facts, protocol and guidelines in various languages and mediums to ensure
  access for those who lack technology.

Low-income residents of the San Gabriel Valley should not live in fear of losing their homes, their jobs, or their
loved ones. We know that if we come together as a community to protect and uplift our most vulnerable, we will
meet the end of this crisis faster and stronger than before.

We understand that you have paramount tasks ahead as you execute and enforce state orders and act on rapidly
changing information. We look forward to partnering and supporting you as you take on these endeavors.

In Solidarity,

Community Leaders of the San Gabriel Valley
   Addendum

Signatories' responses to: What additional needs do you see in the communities that you serve that are not listed above?

f,'ood and Supply Insecurities:
  r  I would like to see better collaboration between State and Federal officials supporting local efforts to address food
  insecurities by providing more opportunities and controlling barriers.
  r  Help for disabled folks or people who have trouble accessing supplies especially with the stores heing empty
  r  Ensure vulnerable individuals have access to proper nutrition through free access to transit or delivery to get
  essential needs, stores rationing/limiting the basic necessities for each customer, senior food delivery, pharmacy pick
  ups and allocating speciflc shopping hours for only seniors and those with special needs.

Housing:
  o Immediate moratorium on rent payments and mortgage payments. Relief for housing costs.
  r Lack of affordable housing ordinance in Alhambra and allowing developers to get rich
  o Allow free street parking while individuals are self-isolating during the COVID-19 pandemic.
  o Shelter for our homeless families
Medical Services:
  r  Ensure medical professionals have enough resources to offer diligent and free COVID-19 testing whether residents
  have symptoms or not in order to stay ahead ofthe capability to provide care.
  .  Access to mental health resources within the community such as one on one counseling and/or group therapy
  services (over the phone or through video) to help members of the community impacted by COVID-I9.
  o Home caregivers are still going to work every day because their households didn't receive any instructions from the
  government about the coronavirus. These are low income workers who rely on high risk public transportation to go
  to work and their jobs to make ends meet.

Other:
  o Locally controlled funding and infrastructure should be reserved from all non-critical projects and made available
  for needs during this unprecedented crisis. All public meetings (e.g., city council and commission meetings) should
  be cancelled until the CDC lifts its current guidance.
  o  We need SGV school superintendents to declare a closure of all schools. Most teachers have children of their own
  to care for. They also need to guarantee payment ofwages to faculty and staff.
  o AYC is able to provide emergency food by appointment - please call 626-537-0954 and, we are looking into how to
  safely provide emergency child care, safe technology access, and meet other basic needs for low-income youth and
  families. Funding to support these services would be very, very helpfull
  r Currently local park restrooms lack hand soap and/or sanitizers. This needs to change.
  o I serve the reentry population, during these hard times we want to make sure that staff at the transition housing are
  taking proper steps to make sure that people under their care have all the basic necessities- access to health care
  services (mental and physical), food, clothing, hygienes, resources, and whatever else deem necessary to ensure that
  they are treated humanely. Resources should also be available for all returning citizens in our community.
  o  We must provide paid holiday leave and hazard pay for all those in the service industry, and other such industries,
  who are forced to work despite frequent contact with people and other risks.

  MINUTES
  MONTEREY PARK CITY COUNCIL
  succEssoR AGENGY (SA)
  SPECIAL MEETING
  MARCH 18,2020

The City Council of the City of Monterey Park held a Special Meeting on Wednesday,
March 18, 2020 at 12:00 p.m. The special meeting was conducted telephonically
pursuant to Executive Order No. N-25-20 issued on March 12, 2020. Accordingly,
Council Members were provided a conference call number and were not physically
present at Council Chambers.

The minutes include items considered by the City Council acting on behalf of the
Successor Agency of the former Monterey Park Redevelopment Agency, which
dissolved February 1,2012. Successor Agency matters will include the notation of "SA"
next to the Agenda ltem Number.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

In accordance with Executive Order No. N-25-20 and guidance from the California
Department of Public Health on gatherings, remote public participation was allowed in
the following ways:

Public comments were accepted in person during the meeting at the West Entrance
(Police/Parking structure) of City Hall located at320 W. Newmark Ave, Monterey Park.

Public comment were accepted by email to mpclerk@montereypark.ca.gov during the
meeting, before the close of public comment, and read into the record during public
comment.

 Public comment may be submitted by telephone during the meeting, before the close of
public comment, by calling 1 (646) 749-3122.Then enter access code 850797317 then
press pound (#). When prompted to enter voice pin press pound (#) again. You will be
joined in the meeting.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Liang called the meeting to order at 12:05 p.m

ROLL CALL:
Assistant Deputy City Clerk Helena Cho called the roll:
Council Members Present: Peter Chan, Mitchell lng, Hans Liang, Teresa Real
  Sebastian
Council Members Absent: Stephen Lam

  The mission of the Gity of Monterey Park is to provide excellent services to enhance
  the quality of life for our entire community

Fire Chief Matt Hallock, lnterim Police Chief Kelly Gordon, Director of Management

AGENDA ADDITIONS, DELETIONS, CHANGES AND ADOPTIONS
None.

ORAL AND  COMMUNICATIONS
None

1. DECLARATION OF EM  NCY: COVID-19 PANDEMIC

  On March 4, 2020, the lnterim Fire Chief provided the City Council an update
  regarding the coronavirus identified as COVID-19. At that time, the City Council
  asked that the City Manager closely monitor the spread of COVID-19 and take
  appropriate action to protect public health and safety. On March 11,2020, lhe
  World Health Organization ("WHO") declared COVID-19 to be a pandemic. WHO
  defines a pandemic as the worldwide spread of a new disease against which most
  people do not have immunity. ln response, the City Manager declared an
  administrative emergency and implemented emergency policies and procedures
  ("EP&P') for mass gatherings, including City Council meetings. The City Council
  must ratify such actions within seven days after the administrative declaration of
  emergency. lf adopted, the proposed Resolution would declare there to be a local
  emergency because of the COVID-19 Pandemic and ratify the actions undertaken
  by the City Manager since March 11,2020.

  CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act)

  The Resolution itself and the actions anticipated by the Resolution were reviewed
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (Public Resources Code $$
  21000, ef seq., 'CEQA') and the regulations promulgated thereunder (14 CaL
  Code of Regulations $$15000, ef seg., the "CEQA Guidelines"). Based upon that
  review, this action is exempt from further review pursuant to CEQA Guidelines $
  15269(a) because the protection of public and private property is necessary to
  maintain service essential to the public, health and welfare.

  Public Speakers:

  Jennifer Tang wrote an email requesting for Council to consider protecting the
  community during the COVID-19 pandemic. She attached a list of
  recommendations on how to support the community during the pandemic.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 12142 declaring a local
  emergency resulting from the COVID-19 Pandemic and ratifying the City
  Manager's administrative Declaration of Emergency dated March 11,2020.

  A RESOLUTION ADOPTED BY THE CITY COUNCIL FOR THE CITY OF
